compliance.emc: 47 CFR Part 15 (FCC) Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55022/EN 55032 Class A; CISPR 22/CISPR 32 Class A; EN 55024; CISPR 24; EN 300 386; VCCI Class A; AS/NZS CISPR 32 Class A; KN32/KN35; BSMI CNS 13438 Class A; EN 61000-3-2; EN 61000-3-3 (datasheet Table 5)
compliance.nebs: designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements of NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 3 (guide Table 30)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 1829 m (6000 ft) at 0 to 40 C for AFO and 0 to 30 C for AFI (guide Table 30; the datasheet's AFI row reads sea level at 30 C)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing, operating and non-operating
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) for AFO; 0 to 30 C for AFI (guide Table 30, datasheet Table 3)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400 GbE QSFP-DD optics and DAC, 400 GbE AOC; QSFP28 100 GbE and QSFP+ 40 GbE with breakout (guide, Network Ports for QFX5130-32CD)
features.optics-sfp-plus: ports 32 and 33 take 10 GbE modules only, not 1 GbE
features.ptp: IEEE 1588 PTP transparent and boundary clock with hardware timestamping (datasheet)

management.oob: one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps

performance.breakout-ports: 64 x 200 GbE + 2 x 10 GbE, or 128 x 100/50/25/10 GbE + 2 x 10 GbE, or 32 x 40 GbE + 2 x 10 GbE (datasheet Table 2)
performance.qsfpdd-speeds: 400 GbE default; 200, 100, 50, 40, 25 or 10 GbE with the matching optic or breakout cable (guide, Setting Port Speed and Channelization)
performance.throughput: up to 12.8 Tbps unidirectional and 25.6 Tbps bidirectional (datasheet Table 2)

physical.weight-note: 24.5 lb (11.11 kg) with power supplies and fans installed (guide Table 31)

platform.cpu: Intel Xeon D-1500 (guide); Intel Broadwell DE (datasheet)

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 12 A at 100 to 127 VAC, 8 A at 200 to 240 VAC (guide Table 19)
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating -40 to -72 VDC, 35 A maximum (guide Table 26)
power.power-measurement-note: Maximum at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers (datasheet Table 4)
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, 1+1, each able to carry the whole switch; both should be installed, on feeds A and B

thermal.airflow-note: AFO is front-to-back (port-to-FRU); AFI is back-to-front (FRU-to-port); no mixing of fans and supplies of different direction
thermal.fans: six fan modules, 5+1; the switch runs three minutes without thermal shutdown while one is replaced

configs.description: QFX5130-32CD-AFI: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules (QFX5220-32CD-FANAI). All have a Juniper azure blue handle and the label AIR IN (guide Tables 3 and 17).
configs.name: ac-b2f

configs.description: QFX5130-32CD-AFO: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules (QFX5220-32CD-FANAO). All have a Juniper gold handle and the label AIR OUT (guide Tables 3 and 17).
configs.name: ac-f2b

configs.description: QFX5130-32CD-CHAS, the spare chassis, shipped without power supplies or fan modules ("Chassis Spare for QFX5130-32CD without FAN & Power module"). Either AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fan modules are ordered separately, and supplies and fans of one airflow only go in. The supply and fan bays are shown open.
configs.name: chas

configs.description: QFX5130-32CD-D-AFI: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.
configs.name: dc-b2f

configs.description: QFX5130-32CD-D-AFO: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.
configs.name: dc-f2b

gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

What the green and amber windows at the corners of the upper (console) RJ-45 jack are. The photograph shows them on both jacks of the stacked shield; the guide describes lamps for the management port only (figure 28, Table 13) and none for the console. Not drawn on the console jack.

The speeds of the management jack. Callout 3 of figure 20 says "100 Mbps/1000 Mbps/10000 Mbps"; the lamp table (Table 13) describes 10 Mbps, 100 Mbps and 1 Gbps. The jack is modelled at 1g, the highest speed Table 13 describes.
The forwarding capacity. The guide's overview says 25.6 Tbps and 5.68 billion packets per second; the datasheet's Table 2 says 5.3 billion packets per second. The datasheet's 5.3 is carried.

The part number of the fan modules. Guide Table 3 and the datasheet say QFX5220-32CD-FANAO and -FANAI; guide Table 17 says QFX5130-32CD-FANAO and -FANAI. Both are listed on each fan component, with the Table 3 and datasheet spelling as its model.

The airflow of JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO. Guide Table 24 prints "Airflow In (port-to-FRU)" for the 32CD row; Tables 3 and 25 and the part number's AFO say port-to-FRU is Airflow Out (front-to-back). Airflow Out is used.
The lower AC input range. Guide Table 19 says 100 to 127 VAC; the datasheet's hardware table says 115 to 127 VAC, and the rating label on the chassis reads 115-127V. The guide's range is carried.

The connector type of the 10M OUT and PPS OUT jacks. The guide calls them "output connectors" and does not name a type; the photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6.8 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated.
The USB revision. The guide says "USB 2.0/3.0 standard" for the one port. The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The vertical rating label at the right end of the rear (an AC input line, a DC input line). It is only partly legible in the photograph and is not drawn.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kits' contracts. The guide names QFX5K-4PST-RMK-E and QFX5220-32CD-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.

chassis.note: guide Table 31 and datasheet Table 2: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.26 in (43.8 cm) wide, 21.1 in (53.59 cm) deep, 24.5 lb (11.11 kg) with power supplies and fans installed, 1RU. The inch figures are used and the centimetre ones in the same cell are rounded copies of them. The width is the body: the rack-requirements table says the outer edges of the front brackets extend it to 19 in, so the brackets are not part of the body and are not modelled. The table does not say whether the depth includes the handles of the supplies and fans.

colour.note: The front plate samples #8a8a8b (median of a bare patch) and the rear panel #7b7e83. The chassis colour is the front's. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's figure 15 draws the rear with orange fans and supplies, and the photograph agrees: it is the front-to-back AIR OUT build, which is the default configuration here. Figure 20 draws the management jacks without lamps; the photograph shows lamps on both, and the photograph is followed.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the rack mount kits QFX5K-4PST-RMK-E (the toolless four-post kit that the switch is installed with in the fast-track procedure) and QFX5220-32CD-4PRMK (a four-post kit), and describes mounting in a four-post rack or cabinet. The library holds no contract for either kit and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 438.4 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-blue-tab.note: A light-blue tab at the lower right, 16.1 mm wide and 6.8 mm high, is the chassis serial number pull-out, callout 7 of figure 20. It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models.

gate-1.note: The front photograph's body, between the left and right edges, is 1910 px wide and 186 px from the top edge to the bottom lip, an aspect of 10.2 against the table's 438.4 / 43.7 = 10.03 (2 percent out: the top lip shows in the photograph). Scale 4.357 px/mm across, used on both axes with the origin at the left edge and the top edge. The rear photograph's body is 1857 px wide, 4.236 px/mm. The guide's figure 14 and figure 20 are half-tone thumbnails and are used only to count and read.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide, published 2026-10-14, states none; the third-party trackers searched list the QFX5130-32CD as supported with no dates. The device states none announced. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the upper left of the face, above the model name QFX5130-32CD. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Right of the SFP+ pair, from the left: a stacked pair of RJ-45 jacks in one shield 16.4 mm wide, a USB-A port standing on its side, and under it the RESET pinhole. Above the jacks the face prints "CON up-arrow, down-arrow MGMT", so the upper jack is the console and the lower the management port, callouts 4 and 3 of figure 20. Each jack shows a green lamp at one corner and an amber one at the other; the guide describes lamps for the management port only (figure 28, Table 13), so the console jack's lamps are not drawn and are a gap. The USB mark is printed above the port. At the left of the face, under the logo, are the 10M OUT and PPS OUT output connectors, two gold coaxial jacks 6.8 mm across, the round ESD point with its warning mark, and the three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID with their legends (callouts 9, 10 and 1 of figure 20).

modules.note: The six fan modules (QFX5220-32CD-FANAO and -FANAI, named QFX5130-32CD-FANAO and -FANAI in Table 17) and the two power supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO and -AFI, JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO and -AFI) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. The guide's Table 3 names the fan modules and the supplies; nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Each supply carries its own small fan inside (the cooling system is six fan modules and a fan in each supply). The status lamp of each fan is on the chassis strip beside its slot (figure 39).

port-lamps.note: Table 8 gives each QSFP-DD port one bicolour lamp and Table 9 gives each SFP+ port two (link and activity at the left, status at the right). The photograph shows two small round lamp windows, stacked 2.9 mm apart, at the left of every pair of columns in each row (2.8 mm left of the pair), and figure 22 draws a leader from each to a cage of the pair: the upper window of a row serves the left column's cage and the lower window the right column's. That assignment is read off figure 22 and is estimated. The SFP+ lamps are two round windows above the upper cage, 5.9 mm apart, and two below the lower one. The lamp heights are read at 3.2 times zoom, estimated to 0.3 mm. The lamps are unlit light pipes in the photograph.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal in the band between the two rows, read off the photograph and figure 22: each column prints "n up-arrow, down-arrow n+1", the even number for the upper cage and the odd one for the lower, so the ports run 0 to 31 down each column and left to right, and the SFP+ pair prints "32 up-arrow, down-arrow 33". The guide numbers the network ports 0 through 31 and the SFP+ ports 32 and 33 (callouts 2 and 8, Table 6). Interface names are not printed. The guide's configuration examples name them et-0/0/N on a single FPC and PIC, always 0 (Setting Port Speed and Channelization), so port N is et-0/0/N and the SFP+ pair is et-0/0/32 and et-0/0/33; that is recorded here and not in an interfaces block, because the face does not print it.

ports.note: Front photograph: 32 QSFP-DD openings in two rows of 16, 81 px (18.6 mm) wide on an 83 px pitch, 19.05 mm against the registry's 19.0, which is used. They stand in eight pairs of columns, the pairs 192.7 px, 44.23 mm, apart, so a gutter of 6.23 mm between pairs: the first opening starts at 38.1 mm, so the 19.0 mm cell starts at 37.78. Counts and groups are the guide's callout 2 of figure 20 and figure 14. Two SFP+ cages stand to the right of the last pair, an upper one at 389.7 mm and a lower one under it, callout 8; they are single cages, not a ganged block.

power.note: Table 19 (AC): 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 12 A at 100 to 127 VAC and 8 A at 200 to 240 VAC, typical 323 W and maximum 839 W. Table 26 (DC): rated -48 to -60 VDC, range -40 to -72 VDC, 35 A maximum, typical 341 W and maximum 871 W. The datasheet's Table 4 gives the same four wattages at 220 to 240 V. The datasheet's note: maximum measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build; the DC pair is carried under its own keys.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.236 px/mm, checked against the guide's figure 15 and figure 41: supply slot 0 at the left end, six fan slots numbered 0 to 5 on a 48.96 mm pitch, then supply slot 1 at the right end, and a grey strip before each supply and fan with its power or fan symbol and number; below the fan number a small round lamp window. The orange fan faces measure 41.1 mm wide and 41.5 mm high; the black supplies 55.2 mm by 41.1. A rating label for the supplies is printed vertically at the right end of the rear, past supply slot 1. Fan 0 is the one nearest the left; the guide's note numbers the fans "starting from the fan closest to the ports", which does not name a side on this face; the photograph numbers them 0 to 5 left to right.

row-pitch.note: The two QSFP-DD openings of the first column measure 12.2 to 21.8 mm and 26.6 to 36.1 mm down, centres 17.0 and 31.35, 14.35 apart; the SFP+ cages 12.4 to 22.2 and 26.4 to 36.3. The registry gives no belly-to-belly row pitch for a QSFP-DD cage, so the photograph's 14.35 is used.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5130 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-10-14, 234 pages (copyright HPE): the front and rear figures 14 and 15, the port panel and management panel figures 20, 22, 24 to 28, Tables 3, 8, 9, 12, 13 (components and lamps), the cooling tables 17 and 18 and figures 33, 35 and 37, the power sections (Tables 19, 23 to 26, figures 41, 43 to 46, 105) and Table 31 (physical specifications). The QFX5130 Line of Switches Datasheet, 1000680-018-EN, July 2025, 9 pages (Juniper Networks): Tables 2 to 4 and the ordering information. Juniper's studio photographs of the 32CD, front and rear (qfx5130-32cd-front-high.jpg, 2100 x 383 px, and qfx5130-32cd-rear-high.jpg, 2100 x 432 px, from juniper.net's image library). Both documents and the photographs are the maker's and public. Nothing in the held intake folder could be read on this host, so no Visio stencil, no 3D model and no other photograph was available; no mechanical drawing or 3D model was found on juniper.net either.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the light latch tongue at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention, read off the device. The SFP+ pair is the same.

variants.note: Datasheet ordering information: QFX5130-32CD-AFI and -AFO (AC) and QFX5130-32CD-D-AFI and -D-AFO (DC), and the spare QFX5130-32CD-CHAS "Chassis Spare for QFX5130-32CD without FAN & Power module". All five share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. NOT MODELLED: the QFX5130E-32CD (-AFI, -AFO, -D-AI, -D-AO, -CHAS), a sibling the guide lists in the same figures and the datasheet in the same tables, which this slice leaves out; the QFX5130-32CD ORv3-compliant switch with tray assembly (QFX513032CDDAFO-T2, 3.64 x 21.14 x 31.4 in), a different mounting for Open Rack v3 racks; and the sibling QFX5130-48C and QFX5130-48CM, whose 48 SFP56-DD ports need an SFP-DD cage that the library does not have (see the pull request).

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band along the top above the cages (about 1.0 to 10.6 mm down), a band along the bottom (about 37.5 to 42.5 mm), a field at the left edge, a column of slots left of the first pair of columns and a field at the right edge. Drawn as vent decor in those positions, pitched to the photograph and estimated.
